docs-parity.why: cheap refuter reading docs against implementation; runs at every posture including baseline because SKILL.md's 'docs are a wave class, not exhaust' doctrine means scheduling it at a deeper tier would reintroduce the doc-lag it exists to prevent (ADR-018)

qa.why: functional exhaustion needs full read-through comprehension of the diff plus entry docs to catch a broken claim; sonnet is the cheapest model that does this reliably

visual-qa.why: screenshot-vs-baseline comparison needs the same comprehension as qa to describe a mismatch usefully; grouped at the same posture tier and routed to the same model as qa

regression.why: writes failing-then-passing tests for findings the fix lane already closed, so it mutates the repo like fix does rather than only reporting; grouped with qa/visual-qa at the same posture tier per ADR-018's routing directive

security.why: two genuinely different toolchains attacking the same code — codex's exploit-construction habits vs opus's design-level trust-boundary reasoning — per ADR-018's cross-provider security routing; disagreement between the two lanes is signal, not noise. `lanes` is the codex-side lane count; `cross`/`cross_template` add the ONE opus lane on a distinct template so its packet is never byte-identical to codex's (no cache-key collision)

a11y._comment: glm is preferred over haiku when the z.ai endpoint is healthy — same checklist-shaped WCAG/axe pass at lower cost; haiku is the safe default routing here because catalogue data can't probe endpoint health at write time
a11y.why: checklist-shaped WCAG/axe pass — a cheap model is sufficient, the value is in running axe-core when available, not in model reasoning depth

supply-chain._comment: glm is preferred over haiku when the z.ai endpoint is healthy — dependency-diff + lockfile checks are mechanical enough for a cheap model; haiku is the safe default routing here because catalogue data can't probe endpoint health at write time
supply-chain.why: diffing a manifest/lockfile since base SHA and checking publish age is mechanical, cheap-model work

polish.why: judging what's worth improving (and distinguishing a real defect from a 'recommend:' redesign idea) needs the same comprehension tier as qa; only runs at the deepest posture where the marginal cost is worth it

perf.why: opt-in only via +perf, never a posture default — it shares qa's browser harness so its marginal cost is low when requested, but per ADR-018's alternatives-considered it's rarely the binding concern on a freshly built feature

docs-sync.why: cheap model is sufficient - the lane reads this run's fixed findings and updates the specific reference-doc claims they invalidate, not open-ended authoring; part of the fixed pipeline (ADR-018 §3), not posture-gated

fix.why: smallest-correct-change remediation across arbitrary file-disjoint groups; sonnet per ADR-018's routing default for the fix stage

reverify.why: re-verify replays the producing finder's own template against the fixed tree, routed to a different provider than whichever lane produced the fix — the adversarial-verify doctrine applied to remediation (ADR-018, SKILL.md 'Patterns ported from the native Workflow tool')
